name: notepadia-pair-programming-prompt
auditedRef: main @ 78bb5ca (the v8.1.0 documentation pass merged on top of G5 @ a0bc020)
auditMethod: Re-read of extensions/notepadia/src (browser, common, electron-main), applications/browser and applications/electron, e2e/ (41 suites), extensions/notepadia/test/, .github/workflows/, docs/ and README.md against the completion ledger of v8.1.0. Every completed task below carries the commit that landed it; every task that v8.1.0 completed was confirmed against the code before it was moved to the ledger.
objective: v8 reached Notepad++ interface parity in the browser, shipped Electron parity and cut a first release; that program is done, so v9 is a verification-and-remediation plan, not a feature plan. Two needs are current and ordered. First, prove and repair real screen-reader accessibility: the app is structurally correct (names, roles, no serious axe violations) but has never been announced by a screen reader, and "structurally correct, unconfirmed in practice" is not shippable for a keyboard-first editor. Second, make every Open/Save dialog start in the user's home folder instead of the server workspace or the current selection. Everything else carried from v8 - the updater proof and the gaps v8 recorded but never scheduled - is deferred and can be done from another terminal without blocking the two current priorities.
primaryConsumer: The repository owner runs the browser build exclusively and works with assistive technology; Electron/macOS/release debt is retained at low priority because the artifact is distributed to others. The owner has asked that screen-reader accessibility be the top priority and that Open dialogs open in the home folder.
rulesCarriedForward: Keep every @theia/* package on the 1.75.0 line. Never add a standalone monaco-editor dependency; use @theia/monaco-editor-core.
Keep product-specific behavior inside extensions/notepadia. Do not fork Monaco, reimplement the filesystem, or replace Theia's command/keybinding/menu architecture.
Improve the browser application first. Electron is touched only when packaging or when a feature is provably Electron-only.
Keep react/react-dom as direct dependencies of application packages.
Do not reintroduce Yarn Berry artifacts (.pnp.cjs, .pnp.loader.mjs, .yarn/unplugged).
Do not claim a build works unless it has actually been built and run.
Extract pure logic into extensions/notepadia/src/common/*.ts and unit test it with node --test in extensions/notepadia/test/*.test.cjs.
Every user-visible feature gets a Puppeteer e2e suite in e2e/ and is added to the SUITES array in e2e/run.cjs.
Commit each task on completion before starting the next one.

Update documentation with each task, in the same commit: README.md ('What is implemented'), docs/usage.md, docs/index.md and CHANGELOG.md. Never batch documentation updates as a separate step done 'at the end' - a task is not 'done' until its documentation describes what the code actually does.
Date-based product versions (YYYY.M.D) generated by scripts/set-build-version.mjs; repo stays 0.0.0; tags are vYYYY.M.D.
newRules: Any new UI must be usable with the keyboard alone and must expose an accessible name. The maintainer's domain is accessibility; a mouse-only toolbar or panel is a defect, not a nice-to-have.

Any new visual styling goes into a single stylesheet layer owned by the extension (src/browser/style/*.css) imported from notepadia-frontend-module.ts, and uses Theia color tokens registered by the Notepadia theme rather than hard-coded hex values scattered in TypeScript. The one existing hard-coded style injection (notepadia-search-mark.ts, document.head <style>) is migrated into that layer.
Browser-hostile keybindings (anything the browser reserves: Ctrl+N, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+Shift+N/T/W) must ship with a working non-reserved alternate and must be documented, not silently broken.

No feature is 'done' because a command exists. Done means: command + menu entry in the Notepad++ position + keybinding + visual affordance (toolbar/status bar/panel where Notepad++ has one) + e2e coverage.

One verb, one target. Any control the user reads as 'Open' opens a file picker on the USER'S OWN disk and is labeled 'Open from Computer' - in the File menu, on the toolbar, in the tooltip, in the shortcut table and in the docs. When a second, different target needs an Open affordance, it is named for that target ('Open from Workspace...'), never 'Open...'. Two entries with the same verb and different destinations is a defect, not a convenience.

Accessibility is the top priority and it is measured, not asserted. A surface is not "done" until a real screen reader has announced it and the session is recorded in docs/accessibility.md. Structure that only the accessibility tree can see (a name, a role, an announcement) must be guarded by an assertion in e2e/a11y.cjs, because a reader that has never run is not evidence.

Open, Save As and Upload dialogs start in the user's home folder. A picker that opens at the server workspace, the last selection or the process working directory is a defect. Where the platform genuinely cannot expose the home path (the browser File System Access API), say so in docs/differences.md and do the closest honest thing; never claim home you cannot reach.

Committed applications/electron/src-gen must embed every preference declared in package.json; scripts/check-preference-defaults.mjs fails otherwise. The release pipeline smoke-tests the packaged binary (scripts/electron-smoke.mjs) before the draft is published. Never tag a release with a stale src-gen - the packaged app then silently drops the preference block.
priorityOrder: P0 - WS-H screen-reader accessibility. Current top priority; the maintainer's domain, and verification rather than features.
P0 - WS-I Open/Save dialogs open in the user's home folder. Current second priority.
P2/P3 - WS-J deferred verification and recorded v8 gaps. Not urgent: G4 can be run from another terminal or machine and does not block WS-H or WS-I.

auditFindings.progressSinceV8: All of WS-A through WS-G in v8.1.0 completed against the browser target between 2026-09-20 and 2026-10-10 (30 of 31 tasks). Only G4 - the updater proof on a real installation - was left open, and it was deliberately deferred rather than unfinished. The full v8.1.0 task text (steps, acceptance criteria, tests) is preserved in prompt/pair_programming_prompt_v8.1.0.json; the ledger below records only the completion commit for each.
auditFindings.headline: Face parity is essentially done: a Notepad++ user opening the browser build today recognizes the window, finds one tabbed Find dialog on Ctrl+F, and finds every menu where Notepad++ puts it. v9 therefore does not add features. It proves the two things v8 could not - that a screen reader can actually use this app, and that the file pickers open where a Notepad++ user expects - and then closes the small set of gaps v8 recorded as prose in its own follow-ups.

A2.title: Strip VS Code shell chrome the browser user should never see

A5.title: Status bar parity and a real INS/OVR mode

workstreams.title: Screen-reader accessibility (current top priority)
workstreams.rationale: F1 made the app structurally correct and then recorded the one thing it could not do: nobody has ever heard a screen reader announce this application. A screen reader exercises the speech and braille path that reading the accessibility tree does not, and the v8 work added many interactive surfaces - the tabbed Find dialog, the Search Results window, Incremental Search, Function List, Clipboard History, the Run dialog, the Column Editor - whose announcements have never been heard. This is the priority.

tasks.title: Verified Orca screen-reader session on Linux, with fixes
tasks.nppReference: Notepad++ is fully operable under NVDA/Narrator/Orca: every control is named and every state change is announced.
tasks.problem: e2e/a11y.cjs and docs/accessibility.md assert the app is structurally correct, but no screen reader has announced it. The reader path is where names, roles, live regions and focus management are actually heard, and the v8 surfaces were never heard. F1 recorded this exact gap ("structurally correct, unconfirmed in practice").
steps: 1. Install and configure Orca with speech-dispatcher on the Linux desktop, and enable Orca speech logging (or run it with a file logger) so announcements are recorded as text rather than only heard.
2. Write docs/screen-reader-test-plan.md as the repeatable script: start the browser build at http://127.0.0.1:3100, launch Orca, and drive the app by keyboard only.

3. Walk and record the whole ring: menu bar (each top-level menu opened), toolbar (Left/Right across every button), document tabs, the editor and the status bar. Record the exact announcement for each stop.

4. Walk and record every dialog and panel: Find dialog (Ctrl+F, each of the four tabs, Count, Find All), Search Results (F7 + Find All), Incremental Search (Ctrl+Alt+I), Function List, Clipboard History, Character Panel, Document List, the Run dialog, the Column Editor and the Summary dialog. Record what is announced on open, on focus move, and on completion (hit counts, mark counts, no-match).
5. Record every place the reader says nothing, repeats itself, announces raw markup (an attribute name, an object, a codicon token), or loses the user's place. Those are the defects.

6. Fix each defect at its source. Likely shapes, to be confirmed by measurement and not assumed: the modeless Find dialog's focus handling; live regions that update before they are in the tree; the status bar group reading all six fields as one string; a dialog that does not move focus on open or restore it on close.
7. For each fixed defect add or extend an assertion in e2e/a11y.cjs so the accessibility-tree regression the fix depends on fails CI if it returns.

8. Replace the "Not yet verified with a real screen reader" paragraph in docs/accessibility.md with the platform, Orca version and what was actually confirmed; keep any genuine upstream gap labeled as such.
acceptanceCriteria: A recorded Orca session on Linux covers the keyboard ring and every dialog and panel listed, with the reader and version named in docs/accessibility.md.
Every surface announces an intelligible name and state; the concrete failures found are fixed, not only documented.
Each fix is guarded by an automated assertion in e2e/a11y.cjs.
tests: e2e/a11y.cjs extended for every announcement defect fixed.
docs/screen-reader-test-plan.md is the manual script a second person can repeat.
tasks.commitMessage: fix(a11y): verified Orca screen-reader session and the defects it found

tasks.title: Verified NVDA session on Windows against the packaged build
tasks.nppReference: NVDA is the default screen reader on Notepad++'s primary platform.
tasks.problem: Windows is the primary distribution target and NVDA is its reader, but neither NVDA nor the packaged Electron build has been driven with a screen reader. Like the updater proof, this needs a Windows machine and an installed build, so it can be done from another terminal or machine while H1 runs here.
steps: 1. Install the latest published release (or the CI artifact) on Windows and launch it.
2. Run NVDA and repeat docs/screen-reader-test-plan.md against the desktop app, including the native Open/Save dialogs and the updater.
3. Record and fix defects as in H1; where Electron differs from the browser, say so explicitly.
4. Record the NVDA version, Windows version and app version in docs/accessibility.md.
acceptanceCriteria: A recorded NVDA session on Windows against the packaged build, with versions named.
Defects fixed, or labeled as upstream.
tasks.commitMessage: docs(a11y): record a verified NVDA session on Windows
tasks.blocked: Requires a Windows machine; not available in this environment.

tasks.title: Extend accessibility-tree and axe coverage to every v8 dialog and panel
tasks.nppReference: Every Notepad++ control is reachable and named; the automated gate should reflect the app's full surface.
tasks.problem: e2e/a11y.cjs runs axe in the default layout, with a menu open, with the Find dialog open and with four panels open. The Search Results window, Incremental Search, Function List, the Run dialog, the Column Editor, the Summary dialog and the Windows dialog are outside the matrix, and none of their interactive controls are asserted to have accessible names. F1's guarantee therefore covers only part of the product.
steps: 1. Add each uncovered dialog and panel to the axe matrix: open it deterministically, run axe, and fail on any serious or critical violation.
2. Add page.accessibility.snapshot() assertions that every interactive control in each surface has a non-empty accessible name, the way the ring stops already are.
3. Keep the one deliberately-tolerated moderate "region" finding documented rather than silently gated.
acceptanceCriteria: Every dialog and panel added during v8 has an axe pass and a named-control assertion.
A newly unnamed control fails CI.
tasks.commitMessage: test(a11y): axe and accessible-name coverage for every v8 dialog and panel

workstreams.title: Open dialogs open in the user's home folder (current priority)
workstreams.rationale: A Notepad++ user pressing Open or Save As expects the picker to start where they live, not at the server workspace, the last selection or the process working directory. Today the browser picker opens at the browser's last location and the desktop dialogs open at the selection's parent folder.

tasks.title: Desktop and Theia file dialogs default to the home directory
tasks.nppReference: Notepad++ File > Open and Save As start in the user's folder.
tasks.problem: NotepadiaLocalFilesContribution calls fileDialogService.showOpenDialog(props) with no folder argument, so Theia's getRootNode(undefined) resolves through UserWorkingDirectoryProvider.getUserWorkingDir(): the parent directory of the current selection when any workspace file is focused, and only home when nothing is selected. A user who has a workspace file selected therefore gets the workspace folder in every native Open/Save/Upload dialog. Save To This Computer... and Upload to Workspace... share the same shape.
steps: 1. Resolve the home directory from EnvVariablesServer.getHomeDirUri() (inject it into the contribution) and turn it into a FileStat (fileService.resolve) to pass as the second argument to showOpenDialog/showSaveDialog. In Electron this becomes the native dialog defaultPath; in the web dialog it becomes the root node shown.

2. Do this for all three routes - Open from Computer, Save To This Computer... and Upload to Workspace... - and for the conflict Save As inside upload, so no Open/Save affordance starts anywhere but home.
3. Keep the decision pure where possible: a small helper that maps "no explicit folder" to the home URI, unit-tested in local-files.test.cjs.
4. Do not regress an explicit-folder caller: the home default applies only where the call currently passes nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: With any workspace file focused, Open from Computer, Save To This Computer... and Upload to Workspace... all open at the OS home directory, not the selection's folder.
The behaviour is identical whether or not a file is selected.
tests: Unit: local-files.test.cjs covers the home-resolution helper.
e2e: assert the dialog service is invoked with a home folder via the same seam the app uses.
tasks.commitMessage: feat(files): native file dialogs open in the user's home folder

tasks.title: Browser pickers resume in the last directory and document the home limitation
tasks.nppReference: Notepad++ File > Open starts in the user's folder.
tasks.problem: In the browser, Open from Computer calls window.showOpenFilePicker({ multiple, types }) with no startIn, so the OS picker opens at whatever the browser last remembered, and Save To This Computer... does the same. Chromium's startIn accepts only a well-known directory (desktop, documents, downloads, music, pictures, videos) or a FileSystemHandle; there is deliberately no "home" value, so a pure-browser first run cannot be forced to $HOME. That has to be documented, not claimed away.
steps: 1. Persist the last directory the user picked, as a FileSystemDirectoryHandle in IndexedDB, and pass it as startIn on the next showOpenFilePicker/showSaveFilePicker so the picker resumes where the user was - the closest the platform offers to "their folder".

2. On the first run, with no remembered handle, pass the closest well-known directory (documents); this is a documented approximation, not the home directory, because the web platform withholds the home path.

3. Record the limitation honestly in docs/differences.md and docs/usage.md: in a plain browser the picker cannot be forced to $HOME; the desktop build and the persisted directory handle are the routes to it. State what happens instead.
4. Unit-test the well-known-directory selection and the startIn-option builder in local-files.test.cjs.
acceptanceCriteria: The browser picker resumes at the last directory the user chose and never silently fails.
docs/differences.md and docs/usage.md say exactly what the browser can and cannot do, and name the desktop path as the way to a literal home start.
tests: e2e: assert the picker is called with the expected startIn option (replace the picker with a recorder, as the Run tests already do for window.open).
tasks.commitMessage: feat(files): browser pickers start in the last directory and document the home limitation

workstreams.title: Deferred verification and recorded v8 gaps
workstreams.rationale: Carried forward from v8.1.0 at low priority. The updater proof is not urgent - the releases are already published and it can be run from another terminal or machine - so it does not block the priority work. These are the remaining gaps v8 recorded in its own follow-ups.

tasks.title: Updater proof: upgrade a real installation (was G4)
tasks.problem: electron-updater is wired and releases v2026.10.9 and v2026.10.10 are published, but no installed build has ever updated itself. Shipping an auto-updater that has never updated anything is the riskiest untested path in the repository. Deferred deliberately: it needs a Windows and a Linux installation and can be run from another terminal at any time, so it does not block WS-H or WS-I.
steps: 1. Install the previous build (for example v2026.10.9) on a Windows machine and a Linux machine and launch it.
2. Use Help > Check for Updates... to pull the newer published release.
3. Confirm the download, the restart prompt, and that the updated app launches at the new version.
4. Confirm latest.yml / latest-linux.yml / latest-mac.yml are served correctly from the release.
5. Document the verified flow in docs/releases.md with the exact versions tested.
6. If the macOS artifact is still unsigned, state in the release notes what Gatekeeper will do and how to get past it.
acceptanceCriteria: An older installed build updates itself to the published release on at least Windows and Linux.
Release notes tell macOS users what to expect from an unsigned build.
tests: Manual on real installations; recorded in docs/releases.md.
tasks.commitMessage: release: verified updater flow for an installed build

tasks.title: Close the gaps v8 recorded but did not schedule
tasks.nppReference: Notepad++ behaviours the recorded follow-ups flag as incomplete.
tasks.problem: Several v8 follow-ups record a real gap and no task to close it: E3's Find in Files... opens the dialog's Find in Files tab but does not prefill the selected folder into the directory field; G1/D2 note that F5, Ctrl+F5 and other browser-reserved chords are only verified in Electron and only their alternates are e2e-covered; C3 recorded that Show Wrap Symbol is not offered and folding is capped at Monaco level 7.
steps: 1. E3 prefill: when Find in Files... is opened from a folder's context menu, seed the Directory field with that folder - a real state hand-off, not a cosmetic default.
2. Desktop chords: verify F5 / Ctrl+F5 (and any other browser-reserved chord) actually run in the packaged Electron app, and add the assertion where it can run.
3. C3 limitations: confirm docs/differences.md states that Show Wrap Symbol is not offered and folding stops at level 7, so they read as deliberate deviations rather than missing features.
acceptanceCriteria: Find in Files from a folder starts with that folder in the Directory field.
Every browser-reserved chord is either proven working in Electron or documented as not offered.
tests: e2e/find-dialog.cjs for the prefill; existing suites otherwise.
tasks.commitMessage: fix(search): prefill Find in Files folder and record reserved-chord behaviour

tasks.title: Distribution hardening: per-user isolation and macOS signing
tasks.nppReference: Notepad++ is a single-user desktop application with no server.
tasks.problem: docs/deployment.md states honestly that Theia 1.75's browser backend has no per-user isolation: one shared filesystem, one shared preference set, no auth. The browser build is distributed to others, so a shared instance is a real deployment shape. Separately, the macOS build is unsigned because no Apple Developer ID is configured, so Gatekeeper blocks it by default.
steps: 1. Decide and document the supported shared-instance story: per-user containers, or an explicit "shared workspace, not a private one" framing.
2. If per-user containers are chosen, provide the compose shape that gives each user their own filesystem and preferences.
3. When Apple credentials become available, configure signing and notarization in the release workflow and verify a signed macOS artifact launches without a Gatekeeper prompt.
4. Until then, keep the unsigned-build warning in the release notes current.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/deployment.md gives a supported, tested shared-instance answer instead of only a caveat.
macOS is either signed and verified, or its Gatekeeper behaviour is stated in the release notes.
tests: Manual / CI on the release artifacts.
tasks.commitMessage: docs(deploy): shared-instance isolation and macOS signing status

executionOrder: Phase 1 - screen-reader accessibility (current top priority). H1 first: a real Orca session on Linux records the defects that matter, and H3 widens the automated gate that guards them. H2 (NVDA) is done from a Windows machine when one is available and does not block H1 or H3.
Phase 2 - Open dialogs in the home folder (current second priority). I1 (desktop / Theia dialogs) and I2 (browser pickers plus the documented limitation).
Phase 3 - deferred verification and recorded gaps, in any order and from another terminal: J1 (updater proof), J2 (the v8 recorded gaps), J3 (distribution hardening).
Commit after each task. Run yarn lint, yarn build, yarn test and yarn test:e2e before each commit. Docs ship in the same commit as the code they describe.
definitionOfDone: A screen reader has announced the running app - Orca on Linux at minimum, NVDA on Windows when a machine is available - the session is recorded, and every defect it surfaced is fixed and guarded by e2e/a11y.cjs.
e2e/a11y.cjs and axe cover every dialog and panel in the product, and every interactive control has a non-empty accessible name.
Open, Save As and Upload dialogs open at the user's home folder on the desktop, and the browser limitation is documented in docs/differences.md rather than claimed away.
The updater has upgraded a real installation on Windows and Linux.
docs/accessibility.md, docs/differences.md and docs/releases.md describe only what was actually verified, with versions and platforms named.
outOfScope: Notepad++ plugin ecosystem and NppExec - replaced by Theia's VS Code extension model per the repository rules.
Full Style Configurator dialog - Monaco theming does not map onto Notepad++'s per-lexer style model; the two themes from A1 plus the standard preference editor are the substitute.
The full ~80-language Notepad++ catalog - the curated 22 stand, per the existing rules.
Code page breadth beyond Windows-1252 and the ISO-8859 family.
Multi-instance mode - Theia is single-instance by design.
Notepad++ Project Panels 1/2/3 - Folder as Workspace covers the common case (E3 step 5).
macOS code signing and notarization - blocked on Apple Developer ID credentials the owner does not have; the workflow already signs automatically the day the five secrets exist.
New Notepad++ feature work. v8 reached interface parity and nothing here adds a feature; v9 is verification and remediation only.

A literal home-folder start in a plain browser. The File System Access API exposes no home directory, so I2 does the closest honest thing and documents the gap; the desktop build is the route to a true home start.
notesForThePairProgrammer: This is a verification plan, not a feature plan. The v8 appearance and feature program is complete (see completedWorkstreams); do not reopen it. The value now is in proving the app works for the people it was built for and fixing what the proof finds.

A screen reader has never run against this app. Everything in docs/accessibility.md up to now was checked through Chromium's accessibility tree and axe, which is necessary but not sufficient. H1 exists to close exactly that gap; treat the first real session as the audit, not a formality.

For the home-folder work, read how the dialog is reached before changing it. The desktop route goes through Theia's ElectronFileDialogService and its getRootNode(folder), where passing a folder becomes defaultPath; the browser route never touches Theia at all and calls the File System Access API directly, which cannot be pointed at home. The two need different fixes and the second needs an honest documented limitation.

When a Notepad++ behaviour cannot be reproduced on the platform, say so in the documentation and skip it. A menu entry that opens an apology is worse than an absent menu entry. This applies to the browser home-folder start in I2.
